old: The conqueror's rising is of two kinds: that beginning with the forest, and that beginning with a single village.
new: The conqueror's rising is of two kinds: that beginning with a forest, and that beginning with a single village.
why: reviewer (minor): Definite article "the forest" is an addition; aṭavī-ādika has no article.

old: And by acts of favour for their own dharma and action, of exemption, of gift and of honour, he should follow what is dear and beneficial to the constituent elements.
new: And by acts of favour for one's own dharma and action, of exemption, of gift and of honour, he should follow what is dear and beneficial to the constituent elements.
why: reviewer (minor): "their" is unmarked: sva- only says "own"; whose dharma (subjects' or king's) is not stated in the compound.

old: by acts of favour for their own dharma and action, of exemption, gift and honour
new: by acts of favour for one's own dharma and action, of exemption, gift and honour
why: reviewer (minor): Same "their own" in the word gloss.

old: अपने धर्म और कर्म के प्रति अनुग्रह, परिहार, दान और मान के कर्मों द्वारा वह प्रकृतियों के प्रिय और हित का अनुसरण करे।
new: अपने धर्म और कर्म के प्रति अनुग्रह, छूट, दान और मान के कर्मों द्वारा वह प्रकृतियों के प्रिय और हित का अनुसरण करे।
why: reviewer (minor): Hindi keeps परिहार here but uses छूट for parihāra in u10 and u11; English is "exemption" in all three. Make one rendering.

old: और देश के देवताओं, समाजों, उत्सवों और विहारों में भक्ति का अनुसरण करे।
new: और देश के देवताओं, सभाओं, उत्सवों और विहारों में भक्ति का अनुसरण करे।
why: reviewer (minor): Modern Hindi समाज means "society"; for samāja (festive gathering/assembly) it misleads.

old: And in the deities of the region, in gatherings, festivals and outings, he should keep up devotion.
new: And in the deities of the region, in gatherings, festivals and amusements, he should keep up devotion.
why: reviewer (minor): GLOSSARY (8.4): vihāra = amusement (विहार). English "outings" departs from it.

old: in the deities of the region, gatherings, festivals and outings
new: in the deities of the region, gatherings, festivals and amusements
why: reviewer (minor): Follow the same glossary rendering.

old: The verb (kārayet, as in 13.5.11) and the object of the non-slaughter (living beings) are not stated; nothing supplied except "[lasting]". rāja-deśa-nakṣatra: "the king's and the country's nakṣatras" (birth-stars), not "nakṣatras of the king and country" as a single compound; Cāturmāsya = the four-monthly seasonal observances, kept as a name.
new: The verb (kārayet, as in 13.5.11) and the object of the non-slaughter (living beings) are not stated; nothing supplied except "[lasting]". rāja-deśa-nakṣatra: "the king's and the country's nakṣatras" (birth-stars), not "nakṣatras of the king and country" as a single compound; Cāturmāsya = the four-monthly seasonal observances, kept as a name. Correction: "birth-stars" is an interpretation, not in the text; rāja-deśa-nakṣatra is read as the nakṣatras of the king and of the country (rāja and deśa a dvandva inside the compound).
why: reviewer (minor): Note says nakṣatras are "(birth-stars)", which is an interpretation not in the text, and the sentence "not … as a single compound" contradicts itself (it describes the same reading as the English).

old: He should prohibit the killing of yoni and young, and injury to virility.
new: He should prohibit the killing of the womb and of the young, and injury to virility.
why: reviewer (minor): "yoni" is left untranslated and "young" is vague, so the English says nothing. Brief: literal rendering plus note when obscure.

new: वह योनि और बालकों के वध तथा पुंस्त्व के उपघात का निषेध करे।
why: reviewer (minor): Singular बाल in Hindi means "hair"; bāla here is "young/immature ones".

old: the killing of yoni and young
new: the killing of the womb and of the young

old: He should have a change of place [made] for those of thievish nature and for mleccha tribes, located in several places, and also for the chiefs of the fort, the country and the army.
new: He should have a change of place, located in several places, [made] for those of thievish nature and for mleccha tribes, and also for the chiefs of the fort, the country and the army.
why: reviewer (minor): The comma placement makes "located in several places" qualify the mleccha tribes; the draft's own note takes anekastham with sthāna-viparyāsam (the change of place).
reviewer (minor): A bahuvrīhi describing persons is not feminine just because prakṛti is; gender is that of the persons (unstated).

reviewer (minor): Gloss "of those wasting after" invents a sense and a genitive; the form -ataḥ before vā is equally acc. pl. (parallel to samarthān) or gen./abl. sg. The sense of anu-√kṣi is not established.

new: pres. part. of anu-√kṣi (?), acc. pl. or gen./abl. sg.
why: reviewer (minor): Case ambiguity should be stated.

old: aparuddha: the glossary sense "prince in disfavour" is not clearly intended here (no prince is mentioned); rendered "shut out" and the technical sense is possible. apavāhita-sthāna lit. "places carried away / removed"; "cleared" is the nearest rendering, and what was cleared is not stated. "pareṇa" = by the enemy.
new: aparuddha: the glossary sense "prince in disfavour" is not clearly intended here (no prince is mentioned); rendered "shut out" and the technical sense is possible. apavāhita-sthāna lit. "places carried away / removed"; "cleared" is the nearest rendering, and what was cleared is not stated. "pareṇa" = by the enemy. Hindi निकाले हुए follows the glossary Hindi for aparuddha; English "shut out" is the literal apa-√rudh (kept off). A person should decide whether aparuddha is one term throughout Book 13. Hindi हटाए गए is closer to apavāhita than English "cleared".
why: reviewer (minor): Draft departs from GLOSSARY (aparuddha = prince in disfavour / निकाला गया राजकुमार) with a reasonable argument (no prince mentioned; pareṇa aparuddha = kept out by the enemy), so "shut out" is accepted for this unit. But Hindi निकाले हुए (expelled) is stronger than English "shut out", and apavāhita-sthāna is "cleared" in English but हटाए गए (removed) in Hindi. Needs a person to fix one term for Book 13.

old: The subject of apavṛtta and upāvṛtta is not stated (the former holder, the constituents or the acquisition); "[it/he]" is supplied. Closing iti not rendered separately. bhūta-pūrva = the second kind of acquisition in 13.5.2.
new: The subject of apavṛtta and upāvṛtta is not stated (the former holder, the constituents or the acquisition); "[it/he]" is supplied. Closing iti not rendered separately. bhūta-pūrva = the second kind of acquisition in 13.5.2. Hindi पूर्व लाभ में supplies लाभ (acquisition) from the threefold list in 13.5.2; the Sanskrit has bhūta-pūrve with no noun.
why: reviewer (minor): Hindi supplies the noun लाभ ("acquisition") unbracketed; English marks the supply as "[case]" and the Sanskrit has bhūta-pūrve with no noun (inferred from the threefold list in u2).

new: Closing iti not rendered separately. "[his]" supplied: the virtues are taken as the father's. The text says pitrye ("in the ancestral") without a noun. Hindi पैतृक लाभ में supplies लाभ (acquisition) from the threefold list in 13.5.2; the Sanskrit has pitrye with no noun.
